beowulf-fitt-23 cruces and guesses (drafter)
1559 þæt [wæs] wǣpna cyst: wæs supplied by Kemble (Grundtvig, query); rendered as printed.
1563 freca Scyldinga: Beowulf (a Geat) called "bold one of the Scyldings"; taken as "fighting in the Danes' cause", a guess.
1564 heorogrim: heoro- read as intensifier ("sword-grim" / "fiercely grim"), same doubt as heorogīfre 1498.
1570 se lēoma: which light (the fire-light of 1516-17 flaring, or a new light at her death) left open.
1574 heard: taken with wǣpen (neut. acc.) rather than with Higelāces ðegn; either is possible.
1585 tō ðæs þe: rendered "to the point that"; alt. "to where". Guess.
1598 þā ðæs monige gewearð: impersonal geweorðan + acc. + gen., "many came to agree"; rare construction, followed from lexica with doubt.
1599 ābroten: MS abreoten; Kemble's ābroten printed (italic o).
1602 sētan: MS secan; Grundtvig sǣton, Grein sētan (italic t).
1604 wīston: read as past of wȳscan "wished" (Klaeber's long ī; editors wȳs[c]ton / wīs[c]ton); not wiston "knew". Guess.
1610 wǣlrāpas: hapax; "pool-ropes" (wǣl "deep water") = ice-bonds on water, a guess; editors wǣgrāpas "wave-ropes".
1617 ættren ellorgǣst: no verb; read as sharing "wæs ... tō þæs" ("the alien spirit so poisonous"); which monster is meant left open; MS ellor altered from ellen.
1619 wīghryre: "war-fall" kept; editors wīggryre "war-terror".
1624-25 sǣlāce ... mægenbyrþenne þāra þe: gen. pl. þāra on a singular noun; editors drop þāra, read þǣre, or sǣlāca. Rendered as printed, loosely.
1630 drūsade: "grew still" from drūsian "become sluggish, subside"; guess on thin evidence.
1634 cyningbalde: hapax; "king-bold, royally brave" a guess; editors cynebalde, Bugge cyningholde "loyal to the king".
1636 ǣghwæþrum: "each of two" with four bearers; rendered "each of them".
1638 wælstenge: hapax; "slaughter-pole", what kind of pole not stated.
1649 þǣre idese: the lady unnamed; queen taken as likeliest (note only).
1650 weras on sāwon: Klaeber/Sievers punctuation (on adverb) kept; earlier editors onsāwon with wlitesēon as object.
